summary: The review focuses on keeping Rust and Cython behavior identical while replacing first-key-only dispatch with composable, safely grouped conditions. The main unresolved risk is how invalid or empty operand lists should behave, especially for @$ where omission is not equivalent to false.

suggestions.title: Use one compositional containment-term primitive in both builders
suggestions.rationale: Both implementations duplicate JSONB operator allowlists and rendering branches in `jsonb_condition`; the Rust path silently wins whenever it returns successfully. Factor the shared conceptual primitive as containment terms, then wrap terms for `@!` and `@$`, while preserving the existing `@>|` output byte-for-byte for single operators.

suggestions.title: Replace first-key dispatch with explicit operator collection
suggestions.rationale: Both current implementations call `next(iter(...))` and reject dictionaries when operator count differs from dictionary length. That cannot render `@!` plus `@$` together. Collect supported JSONB operator entries, render each independently, and AND the resulting groups; return the same skip/handled outcome if any operand is malformed.

suggestions.title: Define mixed comparison/JSONB dictionaries as an explicit rejection
suggestions.rationale: The current paths disagree for dictionaries containing multiple operator classes: Cython checks the first key and then falls through to the last key, while Rust processes only the first extracted entry. A deterministic rule rejecting comparison-token plus JSONB-token mixtures avoids accidental fallback behavior and preserves the existing comparison-token contract.

suggestions.title: Specify empty-list behavior separately for @! and @$
suggestions.rationale: The existing `@>|` helper drops non-list and empty-list operands. Applying that behavior mechanically makes an empty `@!` effectively true by omission, but also makes an empty `@$` true even though OR over zero negated terms is normally false. Add an explicit contract and tests, or reject both forms consistently before release.

suggestions.title: Parenthesize each NOT term and the full OR group
suggestions.rationale: The requested forms are sensitive to SQL precedence once combined with other WHERE predicates. Render `@!` as a parenthesized NOT of the complete OR group and `@$` as a parenthesized OR whose members are individually parenthesized NOT containment expressions; do not rely on PostgreSQL precedence for `NOT col @> ...`.

suggestions.title: Add AST assertions for negation grouping and multi-operator composition
suggestions.rationale: Current tests include an AST grouping check for `@>|`, but most JSONB assertions compare strings extracted from the WHERE clause. Add both-path cases for one and multiple operands, `@!` plus `@$`, and each operator combined with a scalar condition; assert the parsed tree contains the intended NOT/OR/AND nesting.

suggestions.title: Make Rust parity testing fail when the extension is stale or absent in release validation
suggestions.rationale: `PATHS` skips Rust when the extension is unavailable, and `filter_conditions` silently falls back to Cython on exceptions. That permits a release to pass without exercising the implementation that normally wins. Keep the parametrized tests, but add a build/CI validation step that rebuilds the extension and requires the Rust cases to execute before merging.

suggestions.title: Extend the golden corpus through the full build_query format passes
suggestions.rationale: The existing tests verify escaped braces, backslashes, and quotes for positive containment, while the new renderers will repeat literal construction across multiple negated terms. Add negated operands containing all three characters and validate both direct filter rendering and `build_query`, including SQL parsing after placeholder cleanup.
